episode_title: Episode 579 Unlocking Agency Profitability with Niall Cotter

real_qa.q: Why do agency owners struggle to know their profitability per client and service line?
real_qa.r: Complexity grows when agencies scale: when you move to 100 people, you have different layers underneath you with managers managing managers, department budgets, and forecasting assumptions. As you add more people and systems, the founder loses direct awareness. In early stages with 5-10 people, the founder knows every client's margin because he did the contract and costing. But once you pass that information responsibility to others, it becomes diluted.
real_qa.requete: agency profitability per client how to calculate

real_qa.q: What is the difference between avoidable ambiguity and genuine uncertainty in agency finances?
real_qa.r: Genuine uncertainty is economic uncertainty—things you cannot control like political changes, economy shifts, or AI impact. Avoidable ambiguity is understanding your cost to deliver, which is a number finance can work out. There is no excuse, if you have the right governance and discipline, for not being on top of that number and ensuring decisions are consistent with it.
real_qa.requete: avoidable ambiguity vs genuine uncertainty finance

real_qa.q: What are the three key financial ratios agency owners should monitor?
real_qa.r: Payroll as a share of AGI (including everybody loaded), overhead as a share of AGI, and whether cash is moving in line with profit. These three things matter because growth can hide problems in forecasting: you might see profit up year-over-year while your cost to deliver as a percentage of AGI has actually increased.
real_qa.requete: three financial ratios agencies should track

real_qa.q: Why do profitable agencies often report no cash in the bank?
real_qa.r: They are very good at cash flow: they bill retainers in advance so they sit on deferred cash—the projects aren't done, but they have the money in the bank. This was the exact scenario with one founder who said, 'We mastered ensuring we never had to reach out for credit, but at the end of the day, we weren't making any money.' You can be a cash flow expert and profit-poor when it eventually bites you.
real_qa.requete: profitable but no cash in bank agency

real_qa.q: What happened when Niall Cotter discovered hidden costs for foreign consultants at SAP?
real_qa.r: Finance was receiving hundreds of pages of invoices showing legal costs, family costs, health costs, movement costs, and citizenship costs for bringing roughly 200 foreign consultants from India and other countries to supplement work. These costs were not reflected in pricing. After two months of data analysis, Cotter tied down the actual cost, presented the solid number to the sales team, and they renegotiated contracts, ultimately increasing margins by $250,000 annually.
real_qa.requete: SAP foreign consultants costs pricing Niall Cotter

He works with leader-founders who cannot get straight answers to their own numbers, helping them fix financial visibility and decision-making.
